description: Implement Story 1 of the Provider Harness Capability Catalog Plan by adding a truthful OpenAPI capability-manifest vocabulary, migrating the antigravity, claude, and codex manifests with evidence, regenerating derived contracts, and preserving existing provider discovery behavior.

context.customerAsk: Publish a truthful provider capability manifest contract so customers and automation can distinguish harness support from model support, understand ACP posture and modality routes, identify built-in versus configured tools, and trace non-unknown claims to evidence before work is dispatched.
context.problem: Provider metadata cannot distinguish unsupported, conditional, and unknown facts; mixes harness routes with model capabilities; and does not qualify tool availability or evidence. This permits optimistic generic capability claims that can make incompatible harness/model pairs appear executable.
context.solution: Extend the authored OpenAPI model-provider contract and offline semantic validation with explicit support states, evidence records, harness metadata, model-catalog posture, separate harness/model modality routes, and tool availability. Migrate the three native manifests without fact loss, regenerate every derived artifact, and prove discovery parity.

acceptanceCriteria: The Provider Manifest and Provider Catalog schemas accept the complete new vocabulary and reject duplicate facts, dangling evidence references, unsupported route/support combinations, unqualified conditional facts, and direct/tool-mediated output contradictions.

antigravity, claude, and codex express truthful harness, model, modality, tool, and evidence states without losing current IDs, aliases, exact models, efforts, limits, prerequisites, execution capabilities, or response-fidelity facts.
Every supported, unsupported, or conditional modality fact and every supported tool references valid bounded evidence, while unknown remains explicit and requires no fabricated evidence.
Seed claims are published only with primary documentation or checked conformance evidence; unverified Grok/Qwen and later packaged-ACP facts remain unclaimed in this lane.
Existing provider discovery and projection behavior remains unchanged for established facts and deterministic ordering, with focused parity tests proving no fact loss.

Typecheck, focused schema/generator/package/projection tests, API generation and smoke checks pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts are resolved against current main, generated shared files are regenerated rather than hand-merged, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Validate truthful capability facts
userStories.description: As a catalog consumer, I want capability facts to carry an explicit state, scope, route, condition, and evidence so that absent or incompatible facts cannot be mistaken for support.
acceptanceCriteria: Authored OpenAPI components represent native_cli/acp harness kind, typed ACP support metadata, exact/runtime_discovered/operator_selected/unknown model-catalog posture, and supported/unsupported/conditional/unknown capability support.

Harness routes and model facts cover directional text, image, audio, and video and distinguish inline, file_path, implemented ACP resource delivery, tool_mediated, and none mechanisms with applicable media constraints.

Tool facts distinguish built_in, optional, operator_configured, external, and unknown availability and represent nullable default enablement and tool output modalities without treating tool output as direct model output.

Bounded evidence records support primary_documentation, protocol_probe, conformance_fixture, and maintainer_assertion with stable IDs, verification dates, optional URLs/harness versions, and fact references.

Validation rejects duplicate facts, dangling evidence references, out-of-bounds evidence, unqualified conditional facts, non-unknown claims lacking required evidence, invalid route/support combinations, and direct/tool-mediated output contradictions.
Schema and generator tests exercise every enum and representative valid and invalid combinations, including all four support states.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented the additive capability vocabulary and offline semantic validator. Authored OpenAPI components now cover native_cli/acp harnesses, typed ACP support/resource delivery, model-catalog posture, directional modality routes, media constraints, tool availability/output modalities, four-state support, and bounded evidence. Validation covers duplicate and dangling/out-of-bounds facts, conditional qualification, evidence requirements, route/transport compatibility, ACP resource routing, tool-mediated output separation, and direct/tool-mediated output contradictions. Regenerated OpenAPI, Go/TypeScript, catalog schema, published package, and UI-package artifacts. Focused schema/generator/validation/package tests, make test, make typecheck, make api-smoke, provider-catalog-check, model-provider-package-smoke, contracts-check, backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, and vet pass. Native manifest migration is Story 002; discovery parity is Story 003.

userStories.title: Publish truthful native manifests
userStories.description: As a provider catalog user, I want each native provider manifest to distinguish harness and model truth with evidence so that I can interpret its capabilities without optimistic inference.
acceptanceCriteria: antigravity, claude, and codex validate against the new contract and declare native harness posture, exact model-catalog posture, harness routes, model facts, qualified tools, and referenced evidence.
Migration preserves canonical IDs, aliases, exact model IDs, effort values, known limits, discovery prerequisites, maximum execution capabilities, and maximum response-fidelity capabilities.

Antigravity and Codex seed capability statements use supported, unsupported, or conditional only when primary documentation or a checked conformance fixture supports the claim; otherwise they use unknown.
Tool-mediated image or video generation does not create a false direct model-output claim.
Grok, Qwen, and packaged ACP inventory facts are not introduced or upgraded by inference in this story.
Golden catalog tests cover supported, unsupported, conditional, and unknown native modality/tool facts and evidence-reference closure.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Migrated antigravity, claude, and codex to the additive capability contract with native_cli harness posture, exact model-catalog posture, complete eight-route harness matrices, evidence-qualified model modality facts, and qualified tool availability/output facts. Preserved canonical IDs, aliases, exact model IDs, effort values, known limits, discovery prerequisites, maximum execution capabilities, and maximum response-fidelity capabilities. Corrected Codex direct image output to explicitly unsupported while retaining image input support; AGY image generation is represented as tool-mediated output and unknown AGY output routes remain explicit. Added generated-catalog golden coverage for all four support states, availability/default enablement, direct/tool-mediated separation, and evidence-reference closure. Regenerated the published catalog and package metadata. Verification: go test ./internal/providercatalog ./packages/model-providers ./pkg/services/providers/... -count=1, go run ./cmd/providercatalogcheck -root ., make model-provider-package-check, and git diff --check pass. Story 003 remains for the next iteration.

userStories.title: Preserve generated and discovery parity
userStories.description: As an existing provider-discovery consumer, I want the expanded manifest contract to regenerate cleanly without losing established facts or changing discovery behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Canonical OpenAPI changes deterministically regenerate bundled OpenAPI, Go and TypeScript types, manifest/catalog JSON Schemas, generated catalog, and published package artifacts without manual edits.
Generated schemas and language types preserve the authored enum values, required fields, nullability, and evidence-reference semantics.

Provider projection and CLI capability tests prove unchanged identity, deterministic ordering, models, efforts, limits, prerequisites, execution capabilities, and response fidelity while accepting additive metadata.
Static provider discovery stays offline and inert and does not launch providers, probe the filesystem, or access the network.
Focused generation drift checks and the applicable public API smoke check pass from a clean generated state.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
